question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{7}{12}$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{7}{12},$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

To find $\text{E}[XY],$ we use the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}xyf(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}xy(x+y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+xy)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}y]}_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y[\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2}y]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{3}y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{6}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{6}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the covariance formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-(\frac{7}{12})(\frac{7}{12}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{144}.\end{aligned}
$$
